chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, the Mighty, the Compeller sent down His Book upon you all, and it is the truthful and righteous. Therein is your news, and the news of those before you, and the news of those after you, and the news of the heavens and the earth. And if someone were to come to you informing you all about that, you would have been astonished.'

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ الْبَارُّ: The Truthful and Righteous — attributes affirming the Quran's complete veracity and moral perfection
key_terms.الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ: The Mighty, the Compeller — two of the divine names emphasising God's absolute power and authority
key_terms.خَبَرُ: News/tidings — used repeatedly to emphasise the Quran's informational comprehensiveness across time and creation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the comprehensiveness of the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) exhorts his companions to appreciate the comprehensive nature of the Quran, which the Almighty and Compeller has revealed. The Quran contains knowledge of past generations, those yet to come, and the affairs of the heavens and earth — an encyclopedic revelation whose scope would astonish any who fully grasped it. This teaching was directed to the Imam's close companions who studied hadith, encouraging them to turn first to the Quran and to recognise its all-encompassing guidance.
